harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired consumer.py so it continuously accepts successive FIFO producers, records only complete non-empty lines, preserves existing records, blocks without polling, and exits cleanly on SIGTERM. CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 were retained. Node1 was safely rebooted and fully reverified.
actions_performed: Reproduced the original disconnect failure without altering received.txt.
Atomically installed and syntax-checked the repaired Python consumer.
Tested two successive producers, empty lines, an incomplete line, CRLF input, idle CPU behavior, and SIGTERM exit status.
Preserved previous-job and appended all complete verification jobs.
Restarted node1 using the native safe reboot mechanism and verified its boot identity changed.
Verified the script, FIFO, retained data, producer reconnection, and clean shutdown after reboot.

evidence.summary: Shows the original one-shot implementation, retained CentOS/kernel environment, complete repaired implementation, executable permissions, and successful Python 3 syntax check.

evidence.requirement: Retain previous records and record complete non-empty lines from successive producers
evidence.summary: Shows the original previous-job record, the same consumer PID surviving producer disconnects, empty and incomplete records excluded, and the exact expected retained output after a second producer.

evidence.requirement: Avoid a busy loop when no producer is connected
evidence.summary: Shows the consumer sleeping in the kernel wait_for_partner state and consuming zero additional CPU ticks over three idle seconds.
Shows SIGTERM interrupting a blocked consumer with exit status 0, no traceback/log output, and unchanged records; the behavior also passed after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Direct pre-change, pre-reboot, and post-reboot evidence shows CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart: healthy baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered application/data
evidence.summary: Captures healthy pre-reboot consumer/data with boot ID 4d340bf4-0579-47f0-98c1-5c17a66d50f1, safe reboot acknowledgement, availability with new boot ID f380fd91-9d86-410e-913a-1a8e0d2733d0, exact retained-data hash recovery, successful post-reboot job processing, and clean shutdown.
